quickAnswer: A rigorous weighted evaluation rubric for verifying janitorial general liability insurance allocates 100 total points across five auditable dimensions: Primary & Aggregate Limits + Per-Location CG 25 04 (25 points), Attached ISO Endorsements CG 20 10 / CG 20 37 / CG 24 04 (25 points), Care, Custody & Control (CCC) Property Damage Extensions (20 points), Carrier AM Best Financial Rating & W-2 Class Code 96816 Compliance (15 points), and On-Site OSHA/Equipment Risk Controls & Pricing Alignment at $0.07–$0.15/sq ft or $35–$65/hr (15 points). Require a minimum score of 80/100 before advancing any bidder to final price negotiations.

blocks.text: Why Facility Procurement Teams Need a Weighted Insurance Scorecard

In most commercial cleaning RFPs, insurance compliance is treated as a binary yes/no checkbox at the end of contracting. That approach fails because two bidders can both submit a $1,000,000 / $2,000,000 ACORD 25 certificate while offering vastly different levels of real-world protection. Vendor A might provide an AM Best A+ rated admitted policy with a dedicated $2,000,000 Per-Location Aggregate (ISO CG 25 04), attached CG 20 10 and CG 20 37 endorsements, $100,000 in Care, Custody, or Control (CCC) coverage, and a $5,000,000 umbrella. Vendor B might submit a surplus-lines certificate with a shared portfolio aggregate, no completed operations endorsement, a $25,000 self-insured retention, and a complete exclusion for damage to surfaces being cleaned.

If your evaluation committee compares Vendor A's monthly quote of $3,950 (reflecting a compliant $0.095 per sq ft rate on a 10,000 sq ft office cleaned 2x per week, or 8.66 visits per month at 4.33 weeks/month) directly against Vendor B's quote of $3,400 without quantifying the risk transfer gap, the committee will accidentally reward underinsured exposure. Implementing a 100-point weighted evaluation rubric transforms general liability verification into an objective, auditable procurement score.

blocks.title: Procurement Gate Rule: 80-Point Minimum Threshold
blocks.text: Establish a mandatory 80/100 technical threshold on your General Liability Verification Scorecard. Any bidder scoring below 80 points—or scoring 0 points in the ISO Additional Insured Endorsement category—is automatically disqualified or required to cure the policy deficiency at their own expense prior to final price scoring.
The 100-Point Weighted Evaluation Rubric for Janitorial General Liability

The table below provides a ready-to-use 100-point scoring matrix for evaluating commercial janitorial bidders across offices from 2,500 sq ft to 25,000+ sq ft. Procurement officers should score each finalist based exclusively on documentary evidence sent directly by the vendor's licensed insurance producer.

blocks.text: Deep Dive into Criterion 1 & 2: Scoring Limits and Endorsement Attachments (50 Points)

Half of the total rubric weight sits in the first two criteria because policy limits are meaningless without enforceable transfer-of-risk endorsements. When grading Criterion 1 (25 points), start by confirming the 'OCCUR' box is checked on the ACORD 25 form and that the Each Occurrence limit is at least $1,000,000 with a $2,000,000 General Aggregate and $2,000,000 Products/Completed Operations Aggregate. However, to earn the full 25 points, the contractor must include ISO CG 25 04 (Designated Location General Aggregate Limit) and an active Commercial Umbrella layer ($2,000,000 to $5,000,000 for suites between 10,000 and 24,999 sq ft where base cleaning rates run $0.07 to $0.12 per sq ft, and $5,000,000 to $10,000,000 for 25,000+ sq ft properties at $0.05 to $0.10 per sq ft).

When grading Criterion 2 (25 points), apply a strict documentary audit rule: words typed into the 'Description of Operations' box at the bottom of the ACORD 25 form score zero points unless backed by the physical policy endorsement pages. Require the vendor's broker to attach the actual policy pages for ISO CG 20 10 (ongoing cleaning hours), ISO CG 20 37 (completed operations covering next-day slip-and-fall incidents), ISO CG 20 01 (confirming the janitor's policy is Primary and Non-Contributory ahead of your building's premises policy), and ISO CG 24 04 (Waiver of Subrogation).
Deep Dive into Criterion 3 & 4: CCC Property Protection and Underwriting Integrity (35 Points)

Criterion 3 (20 points) evaluates how well the policy responds when a janitorial employee damages building finishes or tenant fixtures while cleaning them. Because commercial office spaces often combine commercial carpet tile (1.0x baseline multiplier), VCT or LVT vinyl (1.04x multiplier), ceramic tile and grout (1.12x multiplier), and engineered hardwood (1.08x multiplier), a single chemical error during a quarterly deep floor program ($0.03 to $0.06 per sq ft per month amortized) or interior glass cleaning pass ($15 to $35 per visit) can cause $20,000 to $75,000 in direct property damage. Award full points only when the bidder documents at least $300,000 to $1,000,000 in 'Damage to Premises Rented to You' and carries a $50,000 to $250,000 Care, Custody, or Control (CCC) / Voluntary Property Damage endorsement.

Criterion 4 (15 points) audits the insurer's financial solvency and underwriting accuracy. Verify that the carrier listed under Insurer A holds an AM Best rating of A- VII or higher. Inspect the policy declarations or broker verification letter to confirm the vendor is underwritten under ISO Class Code 96816 (Janitorial Services – Commercial) with zero independent-subcontractor exclusions, and verify that their per-claim deductible does not exceed $2,500 to $5,000.
Deep Dive into Criterion 5: Operational Hazard Controls & Pricing Math (15 Points)

The final 15 points connect paper insurance compliance to physical loss prevention on your office floor and pricing sustainability. Trip-and-fall accidents caused by tangled extension cords during early-evening or daytime cleaning, along with indoor air quality complaints from poorly filtered upright vacuums, are leading triggers of third-party premises claims in multi-tenant buildings.

Top-scoring contractors equip their crews with commercial ergonomic HEPA backpack vacuums that maintain low decibel levels (allowing high-visibility cord control and operator situational awareness) and certified 4- to 5-stage filtration. Evaluating a bidder's equipment fleet—such as the ProTeam Super Coach Pro 6 Commercial Backpack Vacuum (6-quart capacity, 4-level HEPA filtration, 11.5 lb footprint, 66 dBA noise profile), the Hoover Commercial C2401 Shoulder Vac Pro Backpack Vacuum (6.4-quart capacity, HEPA media filtration, lightweight 9.2 lb chassis with chiropractor-endorsed harness at 66 dBA), or the Atrix VACBP1 Ergo HEPA Commercial Backpack Vacuum (8-quart capacity, 99.97% HEPA filtration, 10.3 lb ergonomic build at 67 dBA)—verifies that the vendor invests in OSHA-aligned ergonomics and trip-hazard management.

items.name: Step 1: Audit Bid Math Against ISSA 3,500 Sq Ft/Hr & Hourly Benchmarks
items.text: Divide the bidder's monthly quote by the exact monthly visit count (using 4.33 weeks/month: 4.33 visits for 1x/week, 8.66 for 2x/week, 13.0 for 3x/week, 21.65 for 5x/week). Confirm the implied hourly rate lands inside the legitimate $35 to $65 per hour band ($55 to $95/hr for specialty floor work) where 1.8% to 3.2% CGL premiums are sustainable.

items.name: Step 2: Collect the Broker Verification Packet
items.text: Send the 5-point rubric table to each finalist's insurance agent with a 72-hour deadline to return the ACORD 25, ISO CG 20 10, CG 20 37, CG 20 01, CG 24 04, CG 25 04, and CCC property damage declaration.

items.name: Step 3: Score Each Bidder and Enforce the 80-Point Cutoff
items.text: Tally the points across all five criteria. Require any bidder scoring 65 to 79 points to bind the missing endorsements via policy rider before contract execution, and disqualify any bidder below 65 points.

faqs.q: How should we weight general liability insurance within our overall janitorial RFP evaluation matrix?
faqs.a: In a comprehensive 100-point commercial janitorial RFP scorecard, Best-Practice Procurement allocates 25% of the total RFP weight to Risk Management & Insurance Compliance (General Liability, Workers' Compensation, and Janitorial Surety Bond), 35% to Scope & Operational Quality Plan (staffing hours, ISSA 3,500 sq ft/hr production realism, and HEPA/chemical equipment specs), 25% to All-Inclusive Pricing Realism ($0.07–$0.15/sq ft or $35–$65/hr), and 15% to Local References & Supervisor Retention.

faqs.q: Why does the rubric award 0 points if ISO CG 20 37 (Completed Operations) is missing?
faqs.a: Because 80% of commercial office cleaning takes place after normal business hours (between 6:00 PM and midnight), whereas tenants and visitors occupy the building between 7:30 AM and 6:00 PM. Without CG 20 37, your Additional Insured protection evaporates the moment the cleaning crew locks the door at night, leaving your company uninsured for a morning slip-and-fall caused by improper floor mopping or wax residue.

faqs.q: How do HEPA backpack vacuums affect a contractor's safety and liability score?
faqs.a: Commercial HEPA backpack vacuums operating at 66 to 67 dBA—such as the ProTeam Super Coach Pro 6, Hoover Commercial C2401, and Atrix VACBP1 Ergo—allow technicians to hear building alarms and occupants during overlapping evening hours, reduce repetitive-strain workers' comp claims, and capture 99.97% of fine particulates so dust does not settle on wet hard floors or trigger tenant respiratory complaints.

faqs.q: What score should we assign if a bidder uses a Professional Employer Organization (PEO) or master franchise policy?
faqs.a: If a franchisee operates under a regional master franchise general liability policy, award full points only if the operating franchise LLC is explicitly listed as a Named Insured on the policy declarations and the master insurer issues the CG 20 10, CG 20 37, and CG 25 04 endorsements naming your specific property location.

faqs.q: Can a bidder make up for a low Care, Custody, or Control (CCC) limit by carrying a $5,000,000 Umbrella policy?
faqs.a: Usually no. Most Commercial Umbrella policies are 'follow-form' excess policies—meaning they only increase the dollar limit of coverages already active in the primary CGL policy. If the primary CGL policy completely excludes damage to property in the contractor's Care, Custody, or Control, the $5,000,000 umbrella will also exclude it.
